غِمْرٌ Concealed enmity and violent hatred, or rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite. (S, Msb, K.) [See also غَمِرَ.] ―
-b2- And (assumed tropical:) Thirst: (S, Msb:) pl. أَغْمَارٌ. (S.) El-'Ajjáj says, “حَتَّى إِذَا مَابَلَّتِ الأَغْمَارَا
” (tropical:) [Until, when they damped their thirst]. (S.) بَلَّتِ الإِبِلُ أَغْمَارَهَا means (tropical:) The camels drank a little. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also غُمْرٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
